title: Poison
text: As the sun set and everything grew quiet. Looking out from my room, it seemed the castle and town were still bustling with people who were still awake. I can hear a distant howl. Siltvelt, the land that never sleeps… it’s quite a challenge, isn’t it? By the way, I heard my Father was almost attacked in his sleep by a vampire and a nightmare demon last night, but Sakura-chan came to his rescue.
“Well… when there are temptation traps around the clock, it actually makes them less interesting, doesn’t it, Motoyasu-kun?”
“Is that so?”

It was the morning of our third day in Siltvelt. Father muttered that. Over the past three days, it seems he’s been subjected to passionate advances from all sorts of pigs coming from all directions. Each time, he managed to escape on his own or with Sakura-chan’s help. Of course, I, Motoyasu, helped out as much as I could.
“I think I’m starting to understand how you feel, Motoyasu. People who approach me with those flirtatious looks are gradually starting to look like pigs to me, too.”
“Naofumi, you’re starting to look at people the way Motoyasu does.”
“I don’t like that at all… I’m getting sick and tired of all these arranged marriage talks at the castle, and I’ve been saying I want to go on a journey to level up.”
“If that’s what you want, I, Motoyasu, will help you fend off any trouble that comes your way.”

“Yeah. I was trying not to mention it because I knew you’d say that. Apparently, the Seven Star Heroes of Siltvelt are coming to meet me at lunchtime today. Once that’s over, it seems I’ll finally be able to move about freely within Siltvelt.”

On the way to our morning meal, my Father explained our plan moving forward to us. Oh, by the way, I’ve been conducting a ecological survey of the Filolial-samas unique to this area. As expected of Siltvelt, it seems there are endemic Filolial-samas found only here, and the messenger who helped escort my Father kindly showed me around the ranch where these Filolial-samas are raised.
“So, will Yuki-chan and the others do their Class Up after that?”
“I suppose so? It’ll be over by early afternoon, so once the Class Up is done, I guess we’ll have to say goodbye to Motoyasu-kun for a while?”
“We can see each other every day through the portal.”
“That’s true. If we set up a base, it’ll be easier to coordinate, and since our levels have gone up quite a bit anyway, the wave should be a breeze, right?”
“I suppose so.”
“Honestly, Motoyasu-kun, I’m so grateful for everything you’ve done to help us.”
“You’re too kind!”
“No need to be so modest. It’s thanks to Motoyasu that I’ve made it this far.”

With that, we arrived at the private terrace reserved for morning meals with my father. Yuki, Kou, and Sakura are here too. The chefs from Siltvelt are placing dishes on plates and setting them out on the table. It seems the leading figures of Siltvelt have gathered here as well.
“Well then, let’s begin our meal.”

After confirming that my father-in-law had taken his seat, one of the dignitaries stood up and made the announcement. Everyone clasped their hands together and murmured something, as if in deep prayer.
“May all be according to the will of the God of the Shield… We have been granted food and life here. May this become the power to carry out the will of the God who protects the world…”
Then they began eating with a clatter of cutlery.
“Sakura-chan, open wide.”
“Open wide.”
The sight of Sakura-chan being fed by my Father is truly heartwarming. It reminds me of my Father and Filo-tan back in the day. I seem to recall a scene like that… or so it feels.
“Sakura-chan, you’re not eating what’s on your own plate—what’s the matter?”
“Huh? Well, it’s poison, and—uh—there’s all sorts of other stuff too.”
Sakura-chan pointed at the plate and glass set out for her.
“…Poison?”

In an instant, everyone present froze in their tracks. Father is holding a spoon close to Sakura-chan’s plate and staring intently at it. Since he’s picked up all sorts of skills along the way, he’s probably using his expertise to identify the poison.
“A fast-acting assassination poison… neurotoxic… no, that’s not all. Expanding the detection criteria to include Filolials…”

Oh! That’s my Father for you! It seems he’s checking for ingredients that are harmless to humans but toxic to Filolials. Come to think of it, Yuki-chan and Kou are also deliberately avoiding certain foods. Such barbaric behavior cannot be tolerated!
“Did Yuki-chan and the others know about this, too?”
“Since we’re all eating together, we just ignore the pain when we eat it.”
“Yeah!”

However, it seems Sakura-chan’s plate was piled high with all sorts of things. What fools they are. Poison has no effect on Filolial-sama. Remember when poison was slipped into the well in Father’s village? Filolial-sama put a stop to that plot as well.
“Is there something on Motoyasu’s plate too?”

Come to think of it, a trace of poison has been laced into Motoyasu’s plate since yesterday. But at this level, if it’s passed off as a unique seasoning, it’s something I can ignore. Besides, I’m a hero, so my resistance to poison is flawless—I won’t flinch at some half-baked poison.
“……What does this mean?”

My father, having set his plate back on the table, scans the room with that same piercing, numbing gaze he used to have. The influential figure from Siltvelt’s expression shifts as if waking from a deep freeze. Even so, Father’s voice is incredibly cold. It’s different from his usual tone—it carries a different kind of intensity.
“How terrifying! Execute the one who served this dish immediately!”
“Is punishing only the person who made it the right course of action!? That’s not right, is it?”
He seems to be reeling from Father’s rebuke.
“Quite so. Attempting an assassination like this, targeting Filolial-sama, is utterly ridiculous! We must carry out an execution that will make them regret ever being born.”
“That’s right. If things had gone wrong, Sakura-chan and the others might have died…”
“Oh! Then let’s flay them alive and let Father witness their agony.”
“Who said we should go that far!? Motoyasu, you really should just stay put.”
“But for the crime of attempting to assassinate Yuki-chan and the others, even ten thousand deaths would be too lenient.”
After that, the room descended into complete chaos. The leading figures of Siltvelt were prostrating themselves before my Father in apology.

Soon afterward, an investigation was launched not only into the meal itself but also into where it had been prepared. My father was seated on the Siltvelt throne, crossing his arms in obvious displeasure. The other day, when he sat on the throne for official duties, he looked troubled—this is quite the contrast.

Incidentally, it seems the assassin was targeting Sakura-chan and me, so Sakura-chan has been placed on my father’s lap, where he’s doting on her in full view of everyone. Doing exactly what the enemy hates. That’s my Father for you. This is how he’ll flush out the enemy.
“Naofumi, more—”
“Ah, yes, yes, just a moment.”
Sakura-chan, in high spirits from being petted, is asking Father to pet her some more.
“I’ll have someone bring the list of suspects right away, so please wait.”
“That won’t do. There’s a possibility they’re thinking of taking the easy way out—like picking on political enemies and getting rid of them.”
“Eek!”
Under Father’s piercing gaze, the senior officials look as if their blood has run cold. Even the representative of the Shusaku clan appears flustered.
“Shield Hero, regarding this attempted assassination… please leave it to us and let us soothe your anger.”
But Father won’t back down an inch.

“I’ve been holding back my anger as long as you didn’t harm us, you know?　Even with those kids who try to set me up on dates or do lewd things around the clock, I’ve been subtly sending them away to avoid causing trouble as much as possible. After all, Siltvelt accepted me, didn’t it? But if someone comes along who thinks they can get close to me by assassinating Sakura-chan—the only woman closest to me—then that’s a whole different story, isn’t it?”
My father rattles off his words at a breakneck pace. Quite right. We mustn’t give our enemies any leeway to strike back.

“I’m being careful with my words here, too—do you really understand that? Or should I put it this way? Anyone who recklessly approaches me and harms those around me—no matter who they are—will pay with their life… No, wait. If I were to say that every single party involved must pay with their lives, would that settle this situation?”
“T-That’s… Please, Shield Hero! Calm down!”
My Father continues, as the flustered elders stand by.

“I think the priority should be to purge as much of the rot from this corrupt country as possible and get it running smoothly—rather than the war with Melromarc… Can I go out there, shout this from the rooftops, and give orders to the Demi-Humans passing by?”
